3) Repo-specific conventions & patterns
--------------------------------------
- Squad-specific conventions (extracted from `.squad/templates/skills/squad-conventions/SKILL.md` and `.github/agents/squad.agent.md`):
  - Zero-dependency Node.js policy for Squad code: avoid adding runtime npm dependencies.
  - Tests (for Squad code) use Node built-in runner: `node --test test/` and `npm test` expected to wrap that. Test files live in `test/`.
  - `.squad/` is the canonical team-state area. Files under `.squad/` (decisions.md, agents/*/history.md, logs) are append-only and workflows expect a `## Members` header in `.squad/team.md`.
  - `.gitattributes` should include union merge driver entries for `.squad/` append-only files (see `.github/agents/squad.agent.md` for exact lines). This preserves append-only logs across merges.
  - Path construction must be OS-agnostic (use path.join in JS, avoid hard-coded separators) to preserve Windows compatibility.
  - Error-handling pattern: use fatal(msg) wrapper (in Squad JS code) to avoid raw stack traces.

- Agent orchestration rules (important for assistant sessions):
  - The Coordinator (Squad) is primarily a dispatcher — it should spawn agents for domain work and not perform domain changes itself (see `.github/agents/squad.agent.md`).
  - Team casting and `team.md` structure are enforced (header `## Members` required).
